extracted.intended_audience: authors and reviewers submitting manuscripts to the BMJ
extracted.subtask_short: submitting manuscripts to BMJ via BenchPress
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for authors and reviewers on using the BMJ's online BenchPress submission system to deposit manuscripts, suggest reviewers, receive acknowledgements, and track editorial/review records. Covers access, security, available help, and record retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit papers via the web (BenchPress)
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors who want to submit a paper to the BMJ are invited to do so via the web (http://submit.bmj.com).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BenchPress is a website where authors deposit their manuscripts and editors go to read them and record their decisions. BenchPress is accessed via http://submit.bmj.com or via a link from bmj.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: System access and security
rubrics_metrics.description: The system is secure, protected by passwords, so that authors see only their own papers and reviewers see only those they are meant to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security controls ensure privacy of submissions and reviewer assignments; reviewers will be invited to access the site to see the relevant paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility (internet and browser required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone with an internet connection and a web browser can use the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No special software is required beyond a web browser and internet access.

rubrics_metrics.name: System provides guidance and required forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The system provides all our guidance and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use the online guidance and forms provided on BenchPress when preparing and submitting their manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors may suggest reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The system allows authors to suggest reviewers for their paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can enter suggested reviewer details within the submission system; these suggestions become part of the submission record for editors to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate acknowledgement of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors get an immediate acknowledgement that their submission has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgement is provided by the system at time of submission, giving confirmation to authors that the manuscript is in the BMJ workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track progress of manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can watch the progress of their manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission record on BenchPress lets authors monitor status changes and editorial actions as the paper moves through review and decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention of submissions and reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the submission, including editors' and reviewers' reports, remains on the system for future reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All correspondence, decisions, and reviewer reports are retained in the system so authors and editors can consult the historical record later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help available from system and editorial office
rubrics_metrics.description: The system itself offers extensive help, and the BMJ's editorial office will help authors and reviewers if they get stuck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If users encounter problems using BenchPress, they should consult the built-in help resources first and contact the BMJ editorial office for additional assistance.
